bead.title: Fix Excel full round-trip type normalization
bead.description:
PROBLEM: A workbook exported by UMFToExcelConverter cannot be imported back through ExcelToUMFConverter.convert() for a minimal valid UMF. Manual verification failed with UMF validation errors because imported columns used Spark type names IntegerType/StringType while UMF.model_validate() requires UMF data_type values INTEGER/VARCHAR/DECIMAL/etc. Existing tests assert helper extraction returns Spark names, but they do not call the full convert() path on an exported workbook.

ROOT CAUSE: src/tablespec/excel_converter.py _extract_columns normalizes raw Excel data types with map_to_gx_spark_type() and stores the Spark/GX type in col_dict["data_type"]. That is appropriate for GX integration but wrong for the UMF import contract. The workbook itself exports UMF type spellings, so export/import should preserve UMF type names.

PROPOSED FIX: Make Excel import return UMF-valid data_type values. Accept UMF spellings and reasonable SQL/Spark aliases as input, but normalize them to UMF names before UMF.model_validate(). Add a full export-to-file then ExcelToUMFConverter.convert() round-trip test that would fail on the current implementation.

In-scope files:
- src/tablespec/excel_converter.py
- tests/unit/test_excel_converter.py
- docs/guide/excel.md only if behavior text needs a small correction

Out-of-scope:
- Advanced-field fidelity for fields not currently represented by the workbook contract.
- Changing downstream Spark/GX type mapping behavior outside Excel import.
- Implementing helper/status UI improvements.
bead.acceptance:
1. test_excel_round_trip_full_convert_preserves_represented_umf_fields: export a rich UMF to .xlsx, import with ExcelToUMFConverter.convert(), assert the result is a valid UMF and preserves table_name, canonical_name, primary_key, column count, column names, UMF data types, length, precision, scale, nullable contexts, descriptions, sample values, format, notes, validation expectations represented by the workbook, relationships represented by the workbook, and file_format if present.
2. test_excel_import_type_aliases_normalize_to_umf_types: workbook rows using INTEGER, VARCHAR, DECIMAL and accepted aliases such as IntegerType/StringType import to UMF data types INTEGER/VARCHAR/DECIMAL, not Spark class names.
3. test_excel_import_decimal_requires_precision_scale: DECIMAL without precision or scale fails before UMF.model_validate() with sheet, row, and field context.
4. Existing extraction tests are updated so they expect UMF type names at the Excel-to-UMF boundary.
5. uv run pytest tests/unit/test_excel_converter.py -k "Excel" passes.
